title.narrative: Strengthening Disability-Inclusive Humanitarian Assistance in Maiduguri and Jere LGAs of Borno

description.narrative: ltpgtPersons with disabilities remain among the most excluded and underserved group affected by the protracted humanitarian crisis in NE Nigeria. They face heightened exposure to trauma, chronic health conditions, and daily mobility and communication barriers. Humanitarian services in Borno continue to fall short of addressing their distinct needs. The NHF 2025 Third Standard Allocation Strategy highlights persistent structural and institutional barriers such as inaccessible facilities, shortages of assistive devices, limited staff capacity, weak referral pathways, and minimal participation of OPDs that consistently deny Persons with disabilities equitable access to life-saving assistance. As a result, Persons with disabilities are too often unable to safely participate in community processes or exercise their rights with dignity.ltbrgtIn response, HALI proposes a transformative, locally led disability inclusive intervention across Maiduguri and Jere LGAs in Borno State. Within 10 months, the project will strengthen access, inclusion, protection, and participation for person with disabilities through a comprehensive package of assistive technology provision, facility accessibility upgrades, inclusive service delivery, structured community engagement, and sustained capacity building of humanitarian actors.ltbrgtThe project will provide essential assistive devices including wheelchairs, crutches, walkers, hearing aids, white canes, and communication boards to 305 persons with physical, earring and visual disabilities which will significantly improving mobility, communication, independence, and access to critical services. In parallel, 9 humanitarian service points will undergo accessibility enhancements, including ramps, rails, adapted signage, and inclusive waiting spaces. These improvements will remove physical barriers that currently prevent Persons with disabilities from safely accessing health and protection services.ltbrgtTo promote disability inclusive action across sectors, this project will advocacy for the domestication of the disability right law for qualitative project sustainability, strengthen referral pathways and enhance frontline staff capacity to deliver inclusive services. Community engagement will be deepened through the establishment of accessible feedback and complaints mechanisms, such as disability sensitive help desks and sign-language support and monthly feedback meetings. The project will also produce inclusive communication materials in braille, large print, audio formats, and pictorial designs to ensure persons with disabilities can access timely, life saving information without barriers.ltbrgtA major focus of the intervention is building sustainable local leadership. A total of 150 frontline government MDA staff and humanitarian staff will be trained on disability inclusion, disability inclusive data collation, AAP, PSEAH and effective communication with person with disabilities. Also the project will mentor 5 OPDs from the DWG for 5 months, empowering them to conduct inclusion audits, participate actively in coordination platforms, and lead grassroots advocacy. Special attention will be directed to persons affected by leprosy in the Molae community of Jere LGA, a group identified by the DWG (2024) as facing some of the most severe stigma, discrimination, and health access challenges among all disability subgroups.ltbrgtTo address urgent medical and livelihood needs, the project will provide cash and voucher assistance (CVA) to 107 persons affected by leprosy, enabling them to access transportation, medical treatment, and essential livelihood support. Additionally, 200 doses of Multi-Drug Therapy (MDT) will be administered to curb the concerning rise in new leprosy infections among recent arrivals in the community. Comprehensive monitoring including baseline, midline, endline, and person with disabilities will ensure adaptive learning, quality assurance, and full accountability to affected population.ltbrgtlt/pgt
